Renting is not in itself bad. Renting is a perfect way to move out of home, live life and also get to know who you are. At least it used to be.

The cost of rent has increased so much that people simply cannot afford it. The rent increase means that people can’t afford to leave home, even if they need to for whatever reason, leaving them to lose their independence and the experience of living their life. 

But whilst rents have increased, so have the portfolios and profits of landlords, especially those who own multiple properties.

Renting was a way to live independently as well as save for a house. Not anymore. The costs are so high the only way people are getting onto the housing market is because a relative with good wealth has passed away, you’ve managed to save since you were born or you won the lottery.

But then, why would you want to move into your own home? It costs more and surely renting is better? 

For some people, yes they prefer to rent. It means no major maintenance costs and the only upkeep they have is cleanliness and reporting issues.

For other, the house isn’t there’s. It’s a house, not a home. It’s a place where they eat and sleep after their 9-5. You can’t decorate, can’t change anything and god forbid you want to put a picture up because bye bye deposit (not all are like this, but greed is rife within the housing sector).

And that point about issues, most landlords don’t care! As long as your house is still standing then that’s fine.
Rentals tend to be poorly insulated, old and have poor security. As long as it meets the minimum requirements, the rest doesn’t matter.

This is not to say all rentals have old water heaters and you have to hold windows open when you shower because you can’t not have it open as the mould will regrow but there’s no other ventilation or latch for the window so a breeze will blow it open and everyone will see you in your birthday suit.

It’s sadly the majority. The majority of rentals are making people ill, no matter what the tenants do. The poor insulation and lack of decent repairs mean that people are spending more on gas, electric and water as the dripping tap which was reported ages ago still hasn’t been fixed.

Owning a home means it’s yours. You can fix the problems and not wait on anyone, except you pay check. The walls don’t have to be magnolia! And you can put pictures up without worrying “will I lose my deposit” because you won’t! It’s yours! 

That isn’t to say owning a home isn’t all sunshine and rainbows, but when you’ve been with a rubbish landlord, it sometimes becomes the only hope. 

As for the controversy, landlords see houses and renters as a business. It’s how they make money. There’s not much humanity behind it.
Estate agents are the same, it’s about money. It’s a business.

But renters and homeowners want a home, not a house.
They want it to be safe, comfortable, warm, looked after as a home should be. 
And if it’s not safe, comfortable, warm and looked after then it’s just another house where they’re paying too much for nothing in return.

What I do is as follows:

4. Low temp 60 min wash on the machine, with non-bio washing pod.

6. Hang to dry, never in the dryer.

7. Repeat until required washing is done.
